lines.text: This is SolarLayout Rooftop, a tool for designing rooftop PV systems in the browser.
You start by entering the coordinates of the roof, or by searching for an address.
When you click the building, its footprint is detected from the map, and you can drag the corners if you need to.
When you build the roof, it appears in 3D with the modules already laid out, and you can show it on the satellite imagery.
If you play the day, you can see how the shadows move, and the shading on every module is calculated for the whole year.
The strings are sized for the inverter you choose, and the stringing options are compared side by side.
Every hour of a typical year is simulated, each loss is listed, and you get the P50, P75 and P90 values.
For the handover you get the report, the single-line diagram, the bill of materials, the cable schedule, and DXF and KMZ files.
For this roof, the result is one thousand one hundred and fifty-five megawatt hours a year.
It is free, with no account needed, at rooftop dot solarlayout dot app.
